label: <DEL> step of longer sequences (L>=6)
explanation: Fires almost only at the delimiter step (90% of activation mass; 55% of all <DEL> steps are active). It never fires in the copy phase or on original positions 0-3. Rate at <DEL> rises with sequence length L (near zero for L=3-4, highest for L=8-9), so (phase==1)&(L>=6) gives dev F1 0.74 and mass recall 0.85. The first token to be copied (out_tok = orig(0)) also modulates it: c,e,x,3,f,d,v,q raise the rate about 2.5x. Adding that condition helped F1 by only about 2 points, so it was left out. The other ~10% of mass is weaker activity on late original-phase steps (orig_idx 6-8) of long sequences, mostly on first occurrences of letters such as a, g, n, i, o. Those activations often ramp up toward the <DEL>. Many <DEL> steps of long sequences still do not fire, so precision is incomplete.
